items.title: Charlie Hardy Interview, 1961-12-16
items.q: And then Souchon was the guitar, and I played the ukulele.

ctx.x: Are the instruments that they played, are they well known, you suppose? Otherwise, I think it would be a good idea to mention.

Well, we had two violinists really, Ray Shack and and Midget Harrison. And we had a mandolin player. We had a tenor mandolin player. Who was the tenor? Shields O'Ranagan. And who was the mandolin? Harry Reynolds. And then Souchon was the guitar, and I played the ukulele. I made the seven pieces. And the reason it was the six and seven eighths was because Harrison was only five foot two, and all the rest was about five foot nine or ten. So we called ourselves the six and seven eighths.
It didn't have anything to do with a hat size then?

items.title: Edmond "Doc" Souchon Interview, 1962-02-17
items.q: And then Charlie Hardy came in with the ukulele.

ctx.x: Then along the line here, I would say around, I must have been no older than 12, maybe 11. We suddenly discovered there were other boys that were playing. We never had gotten together. Everybody was afraid to come out, afraid to show how little they knew. But finally, I went at an invitation to Bob and Harry Reynolds.
